questions.stem: Select the three components of a Filter Condition: (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three components of a Filter Condition are Field (A), Operator (C), and Value (D). This is standard ServiceNow platform knowledge — every filter condition specifies a field to evaluate, an operator (equals, contains, is empty, etc.), and the comparison value. Sum (B) is a mathematical aggregation function, not a filter condition component.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to create and change Service Level Agreements for Vulnerability Response groups?
questions.explanation: The minimum role required to create and change SLAs for Vulnerability Response groups is sn_vul.admin (D). Per the docs: 'Vulnerability managers and senior analysts [sn_vul.vulnerability_admin or sn_vul.admin]: Update properties and vulnerability configurations.' The admin role for VR manages application configuration including SLAs. sla_manager (A) is not a VR-specific role. sn_vul.vulnerability_write (C) manages remediation tasks, not SLA configuration.

questions.stem: Changes made within a named Update Set in a different application scope:
questions.explanation: Changes made within a named Update Set in a different application scope will be captured (A). ServiceNow Update Sets capture customizations across scopes when the Update Set is active during the session. The Update Set records changes regardless of which application scope is active when the change is made. Changes are not excluded (C), partially captured (D), or cause errors (B) simply due to scope differences.

questions.stem: In regard to the Security Operations Process, which of the following statements defines the “Identify” phase?

options.text: What processes and assets need protection?
What techniques can contain impacts of incidents?

questions.explanation: The 'Identify' phase defines: what processes and assets need protection (A). Per the NIST Cybersecurity Framework: Identify = understand assets/processes requiring protection; Protect = implement safeguards (C); Detect = identify incidents (B); Respond = contain impacts (E); Recover = restore capabilities (D). The Identify phase is foundational — knowing what needs protection before implementing controls.

questions.stem: Which module is used to adjust the frequency in which CVEs are updated?
questions.explanation: The NVD Auto-update module (A) is used to adjust the frequency at which CVEs are updated. Per the docs: 'The default day for the NVD update is Weekly on Monday.' The NVD Auto-update scheduled job controls the update interval for CVE data from the National Vulnerability Database. Update (B) is too generic. CVE Auto-update (C) is not the module name. On-demand update (D) allows immediate updates, not frequency adjustment.

questions.stem: If a customer expects to ingest 2 million vulnerabilities during its initial load, which instance size should you recommend?
questions.explanation: For 2 million vulnerabilities during initial load, recommend an XXL instance size (C). Per the docs: 'Validate your instance sizing based on the number of application vulnerable items you expect to import. An undersized instance can lead to long load times.' 2 million records requires XXL-tier resources. L (A) and XL (B) are insufficient. Ultra (D) is for the largest enterprise deployments.

questions.stem: What Business Rule creates a Configuration Item from a Vulnerable Item record?

options.text: Create CI from Vulnerable Group Details
Create CI from Closed Item Details
Create CI from Vulnerable Item Details

questions.explanation: The Business Rule 'Create CI from Vulnerable Item Details' (D) creates a Configuration Item from a Vulnerable Item record. This business rule parses the network and host details within the VI record to identify and create or update the associated CI in the CMDB. Options A (Vulnerable Group) and B (Closed Item) reference incorrect source records. Option C 'Determine CI from Network Details' is a lookup rule, not a CI creation rule.

questions.stem: The components installed with Vulnerability Response include:

options.text: Tables, Scheduled Jobs, Security Operations Common
UI Pages, Business Rules, Vulnerability Scanners

questions.explanation: Components installed with Vulnerability Response include Tables, Scheduled Jobs, and Security Operations Common (A). Per the docs: 'Several types of components are installed with activation of the Vulnerability Response application, including tables, user roles, and scheduled jobs.' Security Operations Common is the shared dependency plugin. Business Rules/Roles/Workflows (B), Properties/Client Scripts/Wizards (C), and Vulnerability Scanners (D) are not the primary installation components.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of Scoped Applications?

options.text: Suppliers can only charge for applications when they are scoped
Scoped applications are scalable, Global applications are not
Scoping encapsulates and protects data and functionality
An application needs to be scoped in order to be deployed as a plugin

questions.explanation: The purpose of Scoped Applications is to encapsulate and protect data and functionality (C). Scoped applications isolate their data, scripts, and UI elements from other applications, preventing interference and enabling clean separation of concerns. This is standard ServiceNow platform architecture. Pricing (A) is unrelated to scoping. Scalability (B) is not the purpose. Plugins can be global or scoped (D is incorrect).

questions.stem: What is the ID associated with the Vulnerability Response plugin?
questions.explanation: The Vulnerability Response plugin ID is com.snc.vulnerability (B). This is the plugin identifier used to activate the application. com.snc.threat.intelligence (A) is Threat Intelligence. com.snc.threat.feeds (C) is Threat Feeds. com.snc.security_incident (D) is Security Incident Response.

questions.stem: Where can you find information related to the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE)?
questions.explanation: CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) information is found at MITRE (B). Per the docs: 'Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE): Dictionary of publicly known information-security vulnerabilities and exposures.' The CVE program is managed and maintained by MITRE Corporation at cve.mitre.org. NIST (C) manages the NVD which enriches CVE data. Tenable (A) and Qualys (D) are vulnerability scanning vendors that consume CVE data.

questions.stem: Filter Groups provide a way to:

options.text: Decouple the use of the grouping from the definition of the grouping
Reuse criteria in a variety of places

questions.explanation: Filter Groups provide all of the above capabilities (D): decoupling use of grouping from definition (A), building criteria once (B), and reusing criteria in a variety of places (C). Per the docs: Filter Groups allow building reusable criteria sets that can be referenced across different application areas. All three benefits (A, B, C) apply to Filter Groups simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which module within the Vulnerability Response application could be used to get information from the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) at any moment?
questions.explanation: The On-Demand Update module (A) is used to get NVD information at any moment. Per the docs: 'You perform CWE updates On Demand from the integration record by default.' The On-Demand Update allows immediate retrieval outside of the scheduled update window. NVD Auto-Update (B) handles scheduled automatic updates, not on-demand retrieval. Vulnerable Software (C) stores software vulnerability data. NVD Patch (D) is not a VR module.

questions.stem: In order for Vulnerability admins to configure integrations, they must have the following Role(s):
questions.explanation: To configure integrations, Vulnerability admins need both the admin role AND integration-specific roles like sn_vul_qualys.admin (D). Per the docs: 'The system administrator [admin] downloads and installs the app. The sn_vul.vulnerability_admin or sn_vul.admin oversees configuration.' Integration setup requires platform admin permissions plus the specific integration admin role. admin alone (A) lacks VR-specific integration access. sn_vul.admin alone (B) lacks platform admin permissions.

questions.stem: In order to more easily manage large sets of Vulnerable Items, what should you create?
questions.explanation: To more easily manage large sets of Vulnerable Items, create Vulnerability Groups (A). Vulnerability Groups organize VIs into logical collections for bulk management, assignment, and reporting. Per the docs: vulnerability groups group items for remediation tracking. Filter Groups (C) are for reusable criteria. Calculator Group (B) is for scoring calculators. Vulnerable Item Conditions (D) define matching rules, not groupings.

questions.stem: This functionality provides a simple way to build criteria once, which can be reused in other platform areas.
questions.explanation: Filter Group (C) provides a simple way to build criteria once and reuse them in other platform areas. Per the docs: Filter Groups allow defining conditions that can be referenced across multiple application contexts. Conditions (A) and Filters (D) are single-use constructs. Favorites (B) save navigation shortcuts, not criteria. Filter Groups specifically support the build-once-reuse-everywhere pattern.

questions.stem: To facilitate the remediation of a Vulnerable Item what type of item is most commonly used?
questions.explanation: A Change request (D) is most commonly used to facilitate the remediation of a Vulnerable Item. Per the docs: 'Create Change: Create a change request or associate a remediation task to an existing change request.' Changes are the standard remediation mechanism in ITSM workflows. The change implements the patch or configuration fix. Problems (A) document root causes. Security Incidents (B) address active threats. KB articles (C) document knowledge.

questions.stem: After closing the Vulnerable Item (VI), it is recommended to:

options.text: Update the values in the Vulnerability Score Indicator (VSI) based on the critically of the Vulnerability
The VI remains active and in place until the Scanner rescans and closes the VI
Mark the CI as exempt from the Vulnerability if the vulnerability was remediated
Compare the Vulnerability with subsequent scans

questions.explanation: After closing a Vulnerable Item, it is recommended to update the values in the Vulnerability Score Indicator (VSI) based on the criticality of the Vulnerability (A). This ensures the risk scoring remains accurate and reflects the resolved vulnerability status. The VI doesn't remain active waiting for rescanning (B) — closing the VI resolves it. Marking CI as exempt (C) is for ongoing exceptions, not post-remediation.

questions.stem: Ignoring a Vulnerable Item:

options.text: Permanently removes the item from the list of Active Vulnerable Items
Move the item to the Slushbucket
Has no impact on the list of Active Vulnerable Items
Temporarily removes the item from the list of Active Vulnerable Items

questions.explanation: Ignoring a Vulnerable Item temporarily removes the item from the list of Active Vulnerable Items (D). The ignore action suppresses the VI from active workflows without permanently deleting it. The item can be un-ignored and will reappear. Permanent removal (A) would require deletion. Slushbucket (B) is not a VI state. The action does impact the active list by hiding the item (C is incorrect).

questions.stem: What do Vulnerability Exceptions require?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability Exceptions require a GRC integration (C). Per the docs: 'Request an exception... using GRC: Policy and Compliance Management' — the GRC Policy and Compliance Management application must be integrated to process vulnerability exceptions. An approval by default (A) may be required but the core requirement is the GRC integration. An Exception Workflow (B) and Filter Group (D) are not specifically required for exceptions.

questions.stem: Approvals within the Vulnerability Application are created based on:

options.text: The sys_approval and the sn_vul_vulnerable_item tables

questions.explanation: Approvals in the Vulnerability Application are created based on the sys_approval and sn_vul_vulnerable_item tables (A). sys_approval is ServiceNow's standard approval tracking table; VR approval records link to sn_vul_vulnerable_item for context. sn_vul_change_approval (C) handles change-specific approvals only. Using only sys_approval (D) lacks the VI linkage. The sn_vul_vulnerability table (B) is not used in approval creation.

questions.stem: When an approval is rejected for a Vulnerable Item exception, what happens to the State field for that record?

options.text: It will be set back to its previous value

questions.explanation: When an approval is rejected for a VI exception, the State reverts to its previous value (D). Per the docs: submitting an exception request transitions state to 'In Review.' Upon rejection, the approval workflow restores the field to what it was before the exception request was submitted. It does not reset to Analysis (A), New (B), or remain In Review (C).

questions.stem: What must Vulnerability Exceptions be supplied by default?

options.text: Integrations with GRC to handle the exception
A manual approval authority for the exception

questions.explanation: Vulnerability Exceptions must be supplied with a reason by default (A). Per the docs: 'Justification: Details related to the reason why this request is being made. This mandatory field must be filled in by the remediation owner.' GRC integration (B) enables policy exceptions but is optional. Requirement Actions (C) is not a standard VR exception field. Manual approval authority (D) depends on configuration.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a Vulnerability Group?

options.text: Groups VIs using a Filter against Vulnerable Item Fields
A Filter defining a sub-set of CIs to be treated as a group
The User Group assigned to resolving the Vulnerable Item
Must have a corresponding filter group

questions.explanation: A Vulnerability Group groups VIs using a Filter against Vulnerable Item fields (A). Per the docs, the VG condition filters records on the sn_vul_vulnerable_item table to include matching VIs. Option B describes CI-based filters, not VI filters. Option C is a team assignment group, not a Vulnerability Group. Option D is not a defining characteristic of VGs.

questions.stem: In order to more easily manage large sets of Vulnerable Items, you would want to create:
questions.explanation: To manage large sets of Vulnerable Items, create Vulnerability Groups (A). VGs organize VIs into logical collections for bulk management, assignment, and reporting workflows. Script Includes (B) are server-side code objects. Filter Groups (C) are reusable criteria sets for cross-application use. Vulnerability Sets (D) is not a VR concept.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the property that controls whether Vulnerability Groups are created by default based on Vulnerabilities in the system?
questions.explanation: The property sn_vul.autocreate_vul_centric_group (A) controls whether Vulnerability Groups are automatically created based on Vulnerabilities in the system. This enables the system to generate one vulnerability-centric group per unique vulnerability, organizing VIs by their parent vulnerability.

questions.stem: What system property allows for the auto creation of Vulnerability Groups based on the Vulnerable Item’s Vulnerability?
questions.explanation: The property sn_vul.autocreate_vul_group_item (C) allows auto-creation of Vulnerability Group memberships based on a Vulnerable Item's Vulnerability. This property associates VIs with their corresponding vulnerability-centric groups automatically. sn_vul.autocreate_vul_centric_group (D) controls group creation itself, while this property controls item membership within groups.

questions.stem: Where in the platform can you create Filter Groups?
questions.explanation: Filter Groups are created via Security Operations > Groups > Filter Groups (D). Per the docs: 'Groups > Filter Groups: Create and use filter groups to locate records from any table on your instance.' The path is Security Operations > Groups, not the Vulnerability module options (A/B/C).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common integration point between Vulnerability and GRC?
questions.explanation: Risk Indicators are the common integration point between Vulnerability Response and GRC (D). VR computes risk scores and exposes them as Risk Indicators that GRC consumes for policy compliance and risk management. Security Incident Response (A), Change (B), and Problem (C) are not the primary VR-GRC integration mechanisms.

questions.stem: To ensure that Vulnerabilities are processed correctly, you can define a Service Level Agreement (SLA) for Vulnerability Response. To achieve this, you would:

options.text: Create a custom workflow to monitor the time between States
Log in as a system admin, and using the globally scoped baseline SLA Modules
Have the role of Vulnerability admin, but only in the Vulnerability Scope
Make sure you have at least the sn_vul.vulnerability_write role and using the baseline SLA Application Modules

questions.explanation: To define SLAs for VR, have the Vulnerability admin role in the Vulnerability application scope (C). VR SLA modules are scoped, requiring the VR admin role within the VR scope. Global admin (B) in global scope cannot access VR-specific SLA configuration. Custom workflows (A) are unnecessary when SLA modules exist. sn_vul.vulnerability_write (D) is insufficient for SLA configuration.

questions.stem: What role is required to view the Vulnerability Overview Dashboard?
questions.explanation: The sn_vul.vulnerability.write role is required to view the Vulnerability Overview Dashboard (D). Per the docs, this role provides access to manage and view vulnerability records and dashboards. A read role (A) provides insufficient access. sn_vul.manager (B) and sn_vul.ciso (C) are not standard VR role names in the platform.

questions.stem: Managers should have access to which role-based data access and visualizations? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Managers should have access to Time period views (B), Up-to-the-minute views (C), and Drill-down to granularity (D). These provide trend analysis, real-time status, and detailed investigation for management oversight. Aggregations for priority and workload (A) are more suited to operational analyst views rather than manager-level reporting.

questions.stem: Filter Group configuration is found under which Application module?
questions.explanation: Filter Group configuration is found under Security Operations > Groups module (A). Per the docs, Filter Groups are listed under 'Groups' within Security Operations, not within the Vulnerability module (B/C/D). The Security Operations > Groups area hosts shared security tooling including Filter Groups used across VR, SIR, and related apps.

questions.stem: Which is the property that is set to True or False based on the customer desire fora popup when creating a Problem or Change record from a Vulnerability or Vulnerable Item (VI) record?
questions.explanation: The property sn_vul.popup (D) controls whether a popup appears when creating a Problem or Change from a Vulnerability/VI record. Per the docs: 'popup property (sn_vul.popup)' is explicitly named. sn_si.popup is the equivalent for Security Incident Response, not VR. Options A, B, C are not valid VR property names.
